review_notes: I read the whole target file and compared it with other files in the repository. Inside the file, the repeated hI/hJ/hK blocks and the nonvanishing transfers along `algebraMap` are short, so I did not report them. The one reportable duplication is across files. The ~45-line argument "nilpotent in M₂(K) gives a pure isotropic vector for ℍ[K,a,b]" appears as `exists_pure_isotropic_of_algEquiv_matrix` in three Sol files: this one, `S_Rat_exists_ternary_eq_neg_prime_of_forall_padic_isotropic.lean` (a near-verbatim copy) and `S_QuaternionAlgebra_nonempty_algEquiv_of_isDefiniteRamifiedExactlyAt_of_prime.lean` (a variant). `natGenerator_eq_of_mem` is also redefined in about nine Sol files with slightly different signatures. It is short, so I did not report it separately, but it could move into the same shared module. I could not check whether the Sol files are meant to be self-contained, or whether the new Theorems module compiles. I did not confirm which of the three Sol files can import it.

findings.problem: This theorem has about 45 lines of nontrivial reasoning: pull the nilpotent matrix unit E₁₂ back to a nonzero N with N² = 0, read off the four coordinates of N², then use 2·re·imX = 0 to force re = 0 and extract an isotropic pure vector. The same argument is proved separately in at least two other solution files. S_Rat_exists_ternary_eq_neg_prime_of_forall_padic_isotropic.lean (lines 15-61) has the same statement and an essentially line-for-line copy of the proof. S_QuaternionAlgebra_nonempty_algEquiv_of_isDefiniteRamifiedExactlyAt_of_prime.lean (lines 404-441) has a variant over a field with (2:K) ≠ 0 that uses Matrix.single and the same re/imI/imJ/imK case split. Any fix to the argument, such as a simp lemma rename, has to be made in each copy.
findings.proposed_change: Put the theorem once in a shared module, for example Theorems/Thm_QuaternionAlgebra_exists_pure_isotropic_of_algEquiv_matrix.lean. Its statement would be `theorem QuaternionAlgebra.exists_pure_isotropic_of_algEquiv_matrix {K : Type*} [Field K] (h2 : (2:K) ≠ 0) (a b : K) (φ : ℍ[K,a,b] ≃ₐ[K] Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) K) : ∃ x y z : K, ¬(x=0 ∧ y=0 ∧ z=0) ∧ -a*x^2 - b*y^2 + a*b*z^2 = 0`. This is the general (2 ≠ 0) form already proved in the nonempty_algEquiv file; the CharZero version follows from `two_ne_zero`. The proof would be the existing one: N := φ.symm (Matrix.single 0 1 1), N ≠ 0 and N*N = 0 by injectivity of φ, then the coordinate equations. In this file, delete lines 18-61 and add the `import Theorems.Thm_QuaternionAlgebra_exists_pure_isotropic_of_algEquiv_matrix`. The call in `exists_pureNrd_eq_adicCompletion`, `exact hiso (exists_pure_isotropic_of_algEquiv_matrix a' b' φ)`, becomes `exact hiso (QuaternionAlgebra.exists_pure_isotropic_of_algEquiv_matrix two_ne_zero a' b' φ)`. The `CharZero K` instance is already available there, so `two_ne_zero` applies. The Rat file and the nonempty_algEquiv file would delete their copies and make the same one-line call, with `h2` supplied from CharZero or from the hypothesis they already have. The shared lemma needs no imports beyond Mathlib.
findings.benefit: Three copies of a fiddly quaternion-coordinate computation become one proof. The single lemma is stated under the weakest hypothesis, 2 ≠ 0. Each solution file shrinks, and its main proof shows the mathematical step (a split algebra gives an isotropic pure vector) instead of re-deriving it.
